_comment: Shared contract fixtures for the inventory metric rules.
metricsCalculator.ts) exist separately so the UI can recompute instantly
without a round trip — this file is what stops them drifting apart, which
is exactly what happened before they were consolidated.
expiryOffsetDays is relative to the moment the test runs; null means the
item has no expiry date at all.
_expectations: stockStatus, per item id — 'low-by-min-stock' is the case that used to
disagree between the dashboard and the alert emails.
wellManaged is everything healthy on stock and not expiring.
'observed_daily_usage' is the rate derived from the household's logged
used INSTEAD of the typed daily_usage by every rule below —
'observed-faster-than-typed' exists to pin that: typed 1/day would give
it 10 days of runway and a 'healthy' status, but the household is
observed to get through 5/day, so it is genuinely low.
_lowStockProbabilityNote: estimateLowStockProbability considers days of runway ONLY, not
min_stock_level — so 'low-by-min-stock' reports the 0.05 baseline even
though its stock status is 'low'. With no consumption it genuinely isn't
on track to run out. Existing behaviour, pinned here deliberately.
have said 10 days and reported the 0.05 baseline)
_wasteRiskNote: Overstock relative to shelf life. A SEPARATE axis from stock and expiry
status -- neither of those meanings changed.
surplus = quantity - daily_usage * daysToExpiry, floored at 0.
No expiry date, zero quantity, or NO KNOWN USAGE RATE -> 0. Already past
the date -> the whole quantity, rate known or not. At risk when
surplus/quantity > 0.10.
A missing usage rate deliberately makes no claim. It used to mean 'none
of it will be used', which flagged every spice, cleaning product and
medicine carrying an expiry date as 100% overstocked.
healthy-1             : 100 - 1*90  = 10 of 100 -> exactly 0.10, NOT > -> safe
healthy-no-expiry     : no expiry date                            -> safe
low-by-days           : 2 - 1*30    = 0                           -> safe
low-by-min-stock      : no expiry date                            -> safe
out-of-stock          : quantity 0, nothing to waste              -> safe
expiring-soon         : 40 - 1*3    = 37 of 40 -> 0.925           -> AT RISK
already-expired       : past its date, none gets used -> all 5    -> AT RISK
no-cost-recorded      : 30 - 0.2*200 = 0                          -> safe
overstocked-perishable: 100 - 0.2*5 = 99 of 100 -> 0.99           -> AT RISK
comfortably-consumed  : 5 - 2*10 = -15 -> 0 surplus               -> safe
dated-but-untracked   : dated, but no usage rate to project from  -> safe
observed-faster-than-typed: 10 - 5*90 -> 0 surplus                -> safe
comfortably-consumed is also low on stock (2.5 days runway). That is the
point: the two axes are independent, and one does not imply the other.
